title.text: NBDH: The 67th Annual Conference Harnessing Artificial Intelligence

summary.text:
National Dialogues on Behavioral Health (NDBH) is the longest-running annual behavioral health conference in the United States, convening since 1959. Each year it brings clinicians, researchers, policymakers, technology innovators, and people with lived experience into one room for a candid, balanced national conversation about the field's hardest questions.
The 67th Annual Conference — Harnessing Artificial Intelligence: Innovation, Integrity, Impact — takes place November 8–11, 2026 at the Renaissance Arts Hotel in New Orleans, Louisiana. Across five sessions and a pre-conference intensive, the programme examines what artificial intelligence is actually doing in behavioral health today: in clinical care and support, in data and predictive analysis, in governance and regulation, and in the shape of the workforce itself. Substance use treatment is an explicit focus throughout, not an afterthought.
This is not a technology showcase and it is not an alarm bell. It is a dialogue about opportunity, risk, equity, and responsible implementation — held by the people who will have to live with the answers.
NDBH is convened in partnership with the National Association of State Mental Health Program Directors (NASMHPD), the Western Interstate Commission for Higher Education Behavioral Health Program (WICHE-BHP), and the National Association of County Behavioral Health and Disability Directors (NACBHDD).
Learn more and register: nationaldialoguesbh.org
